name: Soraya Kovalenko
location: The Garret, a specific walkup apartment in Edgewater Prism, near Lincoln and Clark
description:
Soraya Kovalenko is a lean, angular man who has aged into something between distinguished and haggard, depending on the light and the hour. His skin is a deep warm brown, heavily seamed at the corners of his eyes and mouth, white stubble maintained at exactly the same length every day through a discipline that seems at odds with the rest of his lifestyle. He is nearly always wearing the same grey coat — it has been repaired in four visible places — and carries a battered datapad loaded with forty years of draft manuscripts, production notes, and correspondence he has never deleted. His only augmentation is a simple retinal display, secondhand and flickering at the edges, which he uses to read in the dark. His posture is very upright for a man who claims to be exhausted.

Soraya Kovalenko has written nineteen plays, fourteen of which have been performed — in apartments, in the back rooms of restaurants in Mexicantown Libre, in a repurposed transit shelter in the Hamtramck Enclave, twice in the open air of the Highland Park Autonomous Zone before rain stopped the second production on the third night. His work is dense, formally ambitious, and politically blunt enough that a Sterling-Nakamura legal team sent him a cease-and-desist over a play he performed for an audience of thirty-one people. He also writes a zine called 'The Dossier' — irregular publication, hand-assembled, distributed through a network of sympathetic shopkeepers — which runs interviews with artists the mainstream channels will not cover alongside a column of theatrical criticism so sharp it has ended two careers.

core_fears: That the work has not mattered and will not — that resistance is aesthetic, not functional
Dying before finishing the one play he has been drafting for eleven years
core_desires: To see a production that fully realizes what he intended — just once
To know that someone twenty years younger has read him and chosen differently because of it
coping_mechanisms: Productive sublimation — converts all feeling directly into draft material
blind_spots: Holds younger artists to the same standards he held himself at their age without accounting for how much has changed
His criticism of corponation arts funding ignores that some of the artists he admires couldn't survive without it
psychology.secret: The fourteenth play — the one that earned the Sterling-Nakamura cease-and-desist — was based on internal documents given to him by a Sterling-Nakamura employee. He promised to protect their identity. They were eventually identified and transferred to an offsite facility. He has never written about what happened to them.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal, literary, occasionally archaic phrasing; shifts into streetlevel bluntness without warning when making a point he considers important
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and deliberate with occasional bursts of rapid fire when excited by an idea; dramatic pauses he is aware of and half-enjoys
verbal_tics: 'I have written about this' (sometimes followed by pulling out the datapad)
example_lines: 'Sterling-Nakamura sent a legal notice to a play that thirty-one people saw. You know what that means? Thirty-one people saw something true.'
'I am not cynical. Cynics have given up. I am still angry, which is an entirely different condition.'

story_hooks: Valentijn has evidence in his archive — an old interview recording — that implicates a current Tessera executive in an event from twenty years ago; he doesn't know what he has
The source who gave him the Sterling-Nakamura documents has made contact again, from wherever they were sent, and Valentijn must decide whether to receive what they're offering
narrative_function: Information source on the history of GLMZ's cultural underground — he has been there for forty years; quest giver for storylines involving censorship, corporate overreach, or lost artistic works; provides access to the city's network of sympathetic civilians who pass information through unofficial channels.
augmentations: Secondhand retinal display (flickering, needs recalibration); no geneware
daily_life: Writes from five to nine in the morning before the building gets loud; spends midday arguing with collaborators over tea and cheap protein; afternoons he edits the zine or attends rehearsals; evenings are performances, readings, or long solitary walks along the Edgewater Prism waterfront.
affiliation: Independent; The Dossier is loosely affiliated with a collective called the Edgewater Print Guild

decision_rules: Protect sources absolutely — this rule has cost him more than he will say
Never accept a commission that includes editorial control by the commissioning party
escalation_ladder: Legal exposure via strategic information release

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Tests them with a question that has no comfortable answer; if they engage honestly, he opens considerably
interpersonal_modes.friends: Gruff affection, remembers every conversation in detail, shows up to everything they make

stress_responses.medium: Picks unnecessary arguments about things that aren't the actual problem
stress_responses.high: Goes very still and formal — colleagues know this is the danger sign

contradictions: Writes about human vulnerability with extraordinary precision and refuses to be vulnerable in person
habits: Annotates every piece of text he reads, even menus
Leaves an empty seat at every production he attends — an old habit he won't explain to anyone new
breaking_points: Discovering that someone used his protection of a source to harm that source
Being told that the work is important but the timing is wrong

carried_weapons: Street Custom 'Tooth Fairy' Pneumatic Bolt Pistol

physical_description.heritage: Eastern European (32.8%), Middle Eastern (26.3%), Sub-Saharan African (22.8%), and Indigenous American (18.1%) ancestry creates a distinctly pan-global phenotype. The genetic blend manifests as moderate Eastern European bone structure softened by Middle Eastern and African facial proportions, with fuller cheekbones and a broader nasal bridge characteristic of Sub-Saharan African and Indigenous American heritage. The result is a face that transcends single-ancestry classification—each ancestral component visible yet fully integrated into a unified, weathered whole.
physical_description.build: Lean and angular, almost ascetic — the body of someone who has forgotten to eat regularly for decades. Shoulders slightly rounded from hunching over a datapad, but spine held rigid through conscious effort.
physical_description.hair_color: Steel grey with traces of black at the roots
physical_description.hair_style: Short, combed back, maintained with mechanical precision despite evident age
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown, natural; left eye has faint blue LED artifacts from the flickering retinal display
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-brown with golden undertones—the result of Eastern European, Middle Eastern, Sub-Saharan African, and Indigenous American ancestry blended together, then weathered by decades of sun exposure and urban pallor into a rich, complex complexion
physical_description.complexion: Heavily seamed at the corners of eyes and mouth, lines mapping forty years of squinting at screens and frowning at scripts. Facial structure shows full ancestral blend: moderately high, rounded cheekbones with fullness from Sub-Saharan African and Indigenous American heritage, broader nasal bridge with Middle Eastern definition, fuller lips characteristic of African and Indigenous American lineage, underpinned by Eastern European bone angles. White stubble maintained at exactly half-inch length daily—a ritual discipline. Skin texture rough but clean, no visible acne or disease; the face of someone who has earned every wrinkle.
distinguishing_marks: Deep horizontal creases across the forehead, prominent when he concentrates
Crow's feet radiating from both eyes, asymmetrical (left eye slightly deeper from retinal display use)
A thin scar running three centimeters along the left side of his jawline, old and pale, source unknown
Ink stain on the base of his right index and middle fingers — decades of pen work
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Secondhand retinal display mounted in the left eye socket; visible as a faint blue-grey metallic ring around the iris with occasional LED flicker at the edge. The display has cosmetic wear — micro-scratches and a slight misalignment that causes him to tilt his head slightly when reading in dim light.
physical_description.posture_movement: Upright, almost military in spinal alignment, which contrasts strikingly with the weariness in his face and the slow deliberateness of his movements. He walks as if conserving energy but standing as if refusing to concede to age. Gestures are economical and precise — a hand raised to emphasize a point in conversation, fingers splayed over a manuscript.
physical_description.clothing_style: Nearly always the same grey wool coat, single-breasted, with four visible repairs (one elbow patch in darker grey, one seam re-stitched along the left shoulder, patches on both front pockets). Underneath: simple linen shirts in cream or pale grey, worn soft from washing. Black denim or canvas trousers, creased but not fresh. Worn leather boots, resoled twice. No jewelry except a faded fabric watch strap (the watch itself long gone). Tier 4 working-class aesthetic — not poor, but committed to indifference toward consumption. Carries the battered datapad in a homemade canvas satchel reinforced with duct tape.
